raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Chat derender always returned `role: "assistant"` and ignored `echo`, so it didn't match `/v1/chat/completions` for the same tokens. This fixes that for `/v1/chat/completions/derender` (batch and stream) and adds `--response-role` to generate `output_mode: "derender"` (batch and stream).

Fixes #63356. Related: #56851, #63103, #63148.

**Depends on #63434. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63434#issuecomment-6579638244.**

## Claims

- `/derender` returns the same role as chat: `--response-role` or the last message's role when `add_generation_prompt` is false.
- `/derender` supports `echo` for text content. In batch it's prepended to `content`. In a stream it goes at the start of the first chunk, along with the role.
- Generate `output_mode: "derender"` uses `--response-role`, in batch and on the first chunk of each choice in a stream.
- `vllm serve` and `vllm launch render` both pass `--response-role` to the derenderer.
- Chat serving, batch chat and derender share one implementation of the role and echo logic.
- `add_generation_prompt: false` with empty `messages` returns `--response-role` instead of a 500.

## Validation

New unit tests cover batch (with and without a parser), streaming on the plain and parser paths and generate derender. They fail on `main` and pass with this change.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -q

pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_message_assembly.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out -q
```

`test_derender_parity.py` now runs its server with `--response-role` bot, checks role in every batch case, and adds an echo + continue_final_message case. 

## Details

`OnlineDerenderer` had no `response_role` and hardcoded `"assistant"` in five places. The generate stream added in #63103 hardcoded it too. `echo` wasn't handled anywhere.

The role and echo logic moved into `get_chat_response_role()` and `get_echo_content()` in `message_assembly.py`, next to the shared message assembly from #63148.

Streaming doesn't send echo as its own chunk the way chat does. Each derender call returns exactly one chunk, so the echo goes in the same chunk as the role and `role_sent` already tracks it.
`DerenderStreamState` is unchanged. Clients that concatenate deltas get the same text as from chat.

Known limits:

- `/derender` builds echo from the raw `messages`, while chat uses the parsed conversation. Refusal and thinking parts and multimodal placeholders aren't echoed. This is documented in `derenderer.md`.
- Generate derender can't do echo or the last message's role because `parse_context` doesn't carry `messages`, `add_generation_prompt` or `echo`. It's documented in `token_in_token_out.md` and the wire format question is on #63356.
- Harmony `echo: true` still returns a 500. That's not new and is tracked in #XXXXX.

Small change in coupled chat: streaming echo used to pass list content straight into `DeltaMessage.content` which only takes a string. It's now joined into text like the batch path.

Docs: `derenderer.md` says the render server needs the same `--response-role` as the chat server and explains how role and echo work. `token_in_token_out.md` now lists `derender` as an `output_mode` value.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [ ] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

2. Generate `output_mode: "derender"` still silently ignores `echo` and `add_generation_prompt: false` (only documented). The issue suggested a 400 for these. Was that dropped on purpose, or left for #56851?

## Claude Code Review

🟡 (optional) A derender request with `add_generation_prompt: false` and an empty `messages` list now raises IndexError and returns a 500. Base returned role "assistant". `get_chat_response_role` indexes `request.messages[-1]` without a guard. The derender call sites now run it on client-supplied `chat_request`. `ChatCompletionRequest.messages` has no `min_length`. Fix: return `response_role` when `messages` is empty, or reject it with a 400 at the derender entry point. Either way, an empty list must never reach the index. [also at: vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:162 - A `/v1/chat/completions/derender` call with `chat_request` set to `messages: []` and `add_generation_prompt: false` now fails with a 500.]

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: POST /v1/chat/completions/derender with `chat_request: {"messages": [], "add_generation_prompt": false, ...}`. Nothing validates against this: `messages: list[ChatCompletionMessageParam]` at chat_completion/protocol.py:228 has no `min_length`, and `check_generation_prompt` only rejects setting both flags. In `derender_chat`, online_derenderer.py now calls `self._response_role(chat_request)` before building choices. That calls `get_chat_response_role`, which runs `request.messages[-1]["role"]` and raises IndexError. `derender_chat_response` in scale_out/derender/serving.py only catches `ValueError`, so the client gets an unhandled 500 instead of a response or a 400. On the base branch the derenderer hardcoded `role="assistant"` and never read `messages`, so the same request succeeded.

**Verification:** Trigger: a client sends a derender `chat_request` with `messages: []` and `add_generation_prompt: false`. `get_chat_response_role` (message_assembly.py:84-90) returns `request.messages[-1]["role"]` with no emptiness guard. derender/serving.py:180 catches only `ValueError`, so the client gets a 500. On the base commit the derenderer hardcoded `role="assistant"`, so the same request returned 200.

</details>

🟡 (optional) Derender `echo` can return different text than /v1/chat/completions for the same request, so the parity this PR claims fails for some content parts. `_echo_content` reads the raw `request.messages`, while coupled chat echoes the parsed `conversation`. `get_echo_content` keeps only parts with a `"text"` key. That drops `refusal` and `thinking` parts, which chat parsing turns into text. It also drops the multimodal placeholders that the string content format inserts. Fix: derive the echo text with the same text extraction chat parsing uses (`MM_PARSER_MAP` / `TEXT_PART_TYPES`), so both endpoints produce the same string.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: a request with `echo: true` and `add_generation_prompt: false` / `continue_final_message: true`, whose last assistant message has list content containing a `{"type": "refusal", "refusal": ...}` or `{"type": "thinking", "thinking": ...}` part. Coupled chat (serving.py) calls `get_echo_content(conversation, role)` on the parsed conversation. There, `parse_chat_message_content_part` maps those parts to text via `MM_PARSER_MAP` (chat_message.py:103-116), so the echo includes them. The derenderer (online_derenderer.py:167) calls `get_echo_content(request.messages, role)` on the raw messages. message_assembly.py skips any part without a `"text"` key, so the refusal or thinking text disappears from derender `content`. Image parts under the string content format show the same gap: coupled echo includes the placeholder text and derender does not. test_derender_parity.py only covers plain string content, so it does not catch this. On the base branch derender ignored echo completely, so this mismatch is new with the feature.

**Verification:** The derenderer's `_echo_content` (online_derenderer.py:164-167) calls `get_echo_content(request.messages, role)` on the raw request messages. Coupled chat calls `get_echo_content(conversation, role)` on the parsed conversation. So chat's echo includes the refusal or thinking text, and the derenderer's echo drops it. On the base branch the derenderer ignored echo completely.

</details>

🟣 pre-existing, not blocking: pre-existing: GPT-OSS (Harmony) chat requests with `echo: true` still fail with a 500 instead of echoing, now through the new shared helper. On that path `conversation` holds openai_harmony `Message` objects, not dicts. `get_echo_content` calls `messages[-1].get("role")`, which those objects lack, so it raises AttributeError. Fix: make `get_echo_content` handle every conversation element type, not only Mappings. Either read a Harmony message's author role and text parts, or return "" for any element that is not a Mapping. Plain-dict conversations from `preprocess_chat` must keep working.
_A small fix can ride a push you are already making; otherwise a short reply is enough._

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

For gpt_oss models, `OnlineRenderer.render_chat` takes the `_make_request_with_harmony` branch (vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py:312-314). That branch returns `messages`, a list of openai_harmony `Message` objects, as the conversation (online_renderer.py:587). `OpenAIServingChat` has no Harmony branch around echo, so a POST /v1/chat/completions with `echo: true` passes that list to `get_echo_content(conversation, role)` (serving.py:632 when streaming, serving.py:1062 otherwise). `get_echo_content` evaluates `messages[-1].get("role")` (message_assembly.py:105). `Message` is not a Mapping and has no `.get`, so the request fails with AttributeError and a 500. vLLM elsewhere has to call `to_dict()` on these objects (harmony_utils.py:293-296). On the base branch the inline check `"content" in conversation[-1]` also failed on a non-iterable `Message`. So this is pre-existing, and the refactor that claims to share one echo implementation leaves the path broken. Meanwhile the derender path echoes from the raw request dicts, so gpt-oss chat and derender still disagree.

**Verification:** Trigger: a gpt_oss (Harmony) model gets POST /v1/chat/completions with `echo: true`. So `get_echo_content(conversation, role)` runs `messages[-1].get("role")` (message_assembly.py:105), which raises AttributeError, and the request returns a 500. The base code ran `"content" in conversation[-1]` on the same Harmony Message, which already raised TypeError and returned the same 500.

</details>

+    """Role of the response message: `response_role` (the server's
+    `--response-role`), or the last message's role when the request continues
+    it (`add_generation_prompt=False`).
+    """
+    if request.add_generation_prompt:

+def get_echo_content(messages: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]], role: str) -> str:
+    """Text that `echo` prepends to the response content.
+
+    Args:
+        messages: The conversation, parsed or as sent in the request.
+        role: The response role from `get_chat_response_role`.
+
+    Returns:
+        The last message's text when its role is `role`, otherwise "". Text
+        parts of list content are joined with newlines, as chat parsing does.
+
+    """
+    if not messages or messages[-1].get("role") != role:
+        return ""

🟡 (optional) A derender request with `add_generation_prompt: false` and an empty `messages` list now raises IndexError and returns a 500. Base returned role "assistant". `get_chat_response_role` indexes `request.messages[-1]` without a guard. The derender call sites now run it on client-supplied `chat_request`. `ChatCompletionRequest.messages` has no `min_length`. Fix: return `response_role` when `messages` is empty, or reject it with a 400 at the derender entry point. Either way, an empty list must never reach the index. [also at: vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:162 - A `/v1/chat/completions/derender` call with `chat_request` set to `messages: []` and `add_generation_prompt: false` now fails with a 500.]

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: POST /v1/chat/completions/derender with `chat_request: {"messages": [], "add_generation_prompt": false, ...}`. Nothing validates against this: `messages: list[ChatCompletionMessageParam]` at chat_completion/protocol.py:228 has no `min_length`, and `check_generation_prompt` only rejects setting both flags. In `derender_chat`, online_derenderer.py now calls `self._response_role(chat_request)` before building choices. That calls `get_chat_response_role`, which runs `request.messages[-1]["role"]` and raises IndexError. `derender_chat_response` in scale_out/derender/serving.py only catches `ValueError`, so the client gets an unhandled 500 instead of a response or a 400. On the base branch the derenderer hardcoded `role="assistant"` and never read `messages`, so the same request succeeded.

**Verification:** Trigger: a client sends a derender `chat_request` with `messages: []` and `add_generation_prompt: false`. `get_chat_response_role` (message_assembly.py:84-90) returns `request.messages[-1]["role"]` with no emptiness guard. derender/serving.py:180 catches only `ValueError`, so the client gets a 500. On the base commit the derenderer hardcoded `role="assistant"`, so the same request returned 200.

</details>

🟡 (optional) Derender `echo` can return different text than /v1/chat/completions for the same request, so the parity this PR claims fails for some content parts. `_echo_content` reads the raw `request.messages`, while coupled chat echoes the parsed `conversation`. `get_echo_content` keeps only parts with a `"text"` key. That drops `refusal` and `thinking` parts, which chat parsing turns into text. It also drops the multimodal placeholders that the string content format inserts. Fix: derive the echo text with the same text extraction chat parsing uses (`MM_PARSER_MAP` / `TEXT_PART_TYPES`), so both endpoints produce the same string.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: a request with `echo: true` and `add_generation_prompt: false` / `continue_final_message: true`, whose last assistant message has list content containing a `{"type": "refusal", "refusal": ...}` or `{"type": "thinking", "thinking": ...}` part. Coupled chat (serving.py) calls `get_echo_content(conversation, role)` on the parsed conversation. There, `parse_chat_message_content_part` maps those parts to text via `MM_PARSER_MAP` (chat_message.py:103-116), so the echo includes them. The derenderer (online_derenderer.py:167) calls `get_echo_content(request.messages, role)` on the raw messages. message_assembly.py skips any part without a `"text"` key, so the refusal or thinking text disappears from derender `content`. Image parts under the string content format show the same gap: coupled echo includes the placeholder text and derender does not. test_derender_parity.py only covers plain string content, so it does not catch this. On the base branch derender ignored echo completely, so this mismatch is new with the feature.

**Verification:** The derenderer's `_echo_content` (online_derenderer.py:164-167) calls `get_echo_content(request.messages, role)` on the raw request messages. Coupled chat calls `get_echo_content(conversation, role)` on the parsed conversation. So chat's echo includes the refusal or thinking text, and the derenderer's echo drops it. On the base branch the derenderer ignored echo completely.

</details>

🟣 pre-existing, not blocking: pre-existing: GPT-OSS (Harmony) chat requests with `echo: true` still fail with a 500 instead of echoing, now through the new shared helper. On that path `conversation` holds openai_harmony `Message` objects, not dicts. `get_echo_content` calls `messages[-1].get("role")`, which those objects lack, so it raises AttributeError. Fix: make `get_echo_content` handle every conversation element type, not only Mappings. Either read a Harmony message's author role and text parts, or return "" for any element that is not a Mapping. Plain-dict conversations from `preprocess_chat` must keep working.
_A small fix can ride a push you are already making; otherwise a short reply is enough._

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

For gpt_oss models, `OnlineRenderer.render_chat` takes the `_make_request_with_harmony` branch (vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py:312-314). That branch returns `messages`, a list of openai_harmony `Message` objects, as the conversation (online_renderer.py:587). `OpenAIServingChat` has no Harmony branch around echo, so a POST /v1/chat/completions with `echo: true` passes that list to `get_echo_content(conversation, role)` (serving.py:632 when streaming, serving.py:1062 otherwise). `get_echo_content` evaluates `messages[-1].get("role")` (message_assembly.py:105). `Message` is not a Mapping and has no `.get`, so the request fails with AttributeError and a 500. vLLM elsewhere has to call `to_dict()` on these objects (harmony_utils.py:293-296). On the base branch the inline check `"content" in conversation[-1]` also failed on a non-iterable `Message`. So this is pre-existing, and the refactor that claims to share one echo implementation leaves the path broken. Meanwhile the derender path echoes from the raw request dicts, so gpt-oss chat and derender still disagree.

**Verification:** Trigger: a gpt_oss (Harmony) model gets POST /v1/chat/completions with `echo: true`. So `get_echo_content(conversation, role)` runs `messages[-1].get("role")` (message_assembly.py:105), which raises AttributeError, and the request returns a 500. The base code ran `"content" in conversation[-1]` on the same Harmony Message, which already raised TypeError and returned the same 500.

</details>
